gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-work-sans: Soft, snug, and friendly: Rounded Elegance sets its letters almost touching, with one steady line throughout. And Work Sans keeps its own build just as simple, leaving c tips well apart and a high mean line above.
gen-dafont-sansumi-fs-supreme: Sansumi spaces its flat, unshaded letters as widely as ticks on a tape measure, with a first capital that barely rises. Supreme sets a heavy, open-mouthed band beneath it.
gen-dafont-sansumi-manrope: Manrope reads bright and open, every curve leaving a generous gap at its mouth and the capitals barely stepping above lowercase. Sansumi's wide, flat lettering sits above it easily.
gen-dafont-sansumi-satoshi: Sansumi spreads flat, unshaded letters wide apart, its first capital barely rising above the rest. Then Satoshi follows in a plain sans with a soaring x-height and an open e, cut to one width.
gen-dafont-sansumi-work-sans: Work Sans reads crisply, its c tips held well apart and its mean line sitting high on the sans. But Sansumi is the one for wide, flat spacing, while Work Sans handles steady text.
gen-dafont-stilu-archivo: Refined is the first word for Stilu, whose bowls swell tall like blown glass and whose line width never shifts. And Archivo brings a commanding x-height and outward-opening curves, which gives the pair its strongest quality.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-alpino: Stilu leads with tall, glassy bowls and open terminals. Alpino sits underneath as a plain sans, tightly spaced and tall in the body, so its ascenders look short beside that luxurious heading.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-bespoke-slab: Glassy, tall, and unshaded, Stilu looks luxurious even in a single line weight. Bespoke Slab follows as a text serif with tall lowercase bodies, while Stilu earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-literata: Literata brings sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones to the serif, with curved letters left wide open at the mouth. Stilu's smooth, unswelling outlines lead above it, and the text feels bookish.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-supreme: Stilu draws its letters as a thread of ink, with tall bowls like blown glass and no tapering. Then Supreme settles into a heavier, crisp band of sans-serif text that stays open and easy to follow.
